title: Healthy eating on RM15 a day for working women
intro: Yes, with RM15 a day you can still get enough protein and vegetables while losing weight. The secret is to combine smart eating out with a bit of food from home.

sections.p: Breakfast from home: 2 eggs and bread, estimated RM2-3. Nasi campur for lunch: half portion of rice, 1 protein dish, 2 vegetables, estimated RM7-9. Dinner at home: eggs, tempeh or fish with vegetables, estimated RM3-4. Prices differ by area, so this is only an estimate.
Eggs, tofu, tempeh, ikan kembung, ikan bilis, dhal and chicken thigh are all wallet-friendly. One tray of eggs can last a week for breakfast and dinner. Enough protein helps you stay full longer.

Vegetables are usually cheap at nasi campur stalls. Take two types of vegetables and one chicken or fish dish. Dishes fried in batter or with lots of santan gravy are usually more expensive and higher in calories.
Sweet drinks every day can cost you RM3-5 and an estimated 150-250 kcal per glass. Bring your own water bottle. If you want to drink at a shop, choose teh O ais kosong or kopi kurang manis.
Bananas, boiled peanuts, boiled corn or boiled eggs are cheaper than cakes and kuih from cafés. Buy fruit at the pasar malam or supermarket when prices are low.

action: Buy one tray of eggs and one pack of tempeh or tofu this week.
Bring your own water bottle to work every day.
Bring a packed lunch at least 2 days a week.
Track your food spending for 5 days to see where your money is leaking.
myth: Many people believe healthy eating must be expensive and needs imported food. Actually, local food like eggs, tempeh, ikan kembung and vegetables from the market is enough to lose weight.

faq.q: Is RM15 enough if I live in KL?
faq.a: It's more challenging, but possible if breakfast and dinner are from home. Lunch around the office might be RM10-12, so bringing a packed lunch 2-3 times a week helps a lot.

faq.q: I don't have a full kitchen, only a rice cooker.
faq.a: A rice cooker can steam eggs, chicken and vegetables together with the rice. Add soy sauce or sambal for flavour. That's already a complete meal.

faq.q: Do I need to buy the more expensive chicken breast?
faq.a: No need. Skinless chicken thigh, ikan kembung, eggs and tempeh are also good protein sources and cheaper.
